explore_prose: Every run in this experiment is in the explorer below: filter by outcome to see which settings held the SLOs, or by setting to compare one sweep against another.
Each sweep's hypothesis was written before the runs, and is quoted beside that sweep's measured result below.

hero.html: 322 configurations over 4 sweeps (colocated, pd-dp1, pd-dp2, pd-always), each at 5 load levels, every run on exactly 64 GPUs.
8x TP4xDP2 + EP (batch tokens 32,768), from the colocated sweep, reached 54.24 tok/s/GPU (3471.4 tok/s across the fleet) at concurrency 64 while holding the scenario's SLOs.
8x TP4xDP2 + EP (batch tokens 32,768) at concurrency 64. 603 of 1610 runs held the SLOs.

meta: deterministic sweep — no LLM in the measurement path
recommendation_prose: The table below ranks the measured operating points by output tok/s per GPU, the objective this experiment selects on, among runs that held the scenario's SLOs.

prose: The colocated control should hold ITL only with a chunked-prefill cap, and the wide-dp shapes should give the most tokens per GPU.
Measured: best was 8x TP4xDP2 + EP (batch tokens 32,768) at 54.24 tok/s/GPU (concurrency 64).
sections.title: Sweep: colocated

prose: Prefill-heavy ratios should win on 10k prompts, and a threshold near the median prompt should beat splitting every request.
Measured: best was 2P/6D TP8 + EP at 41.72 tok/s/GPU (concurrency 32).
sections.title: Sweep: pd-dp1

prose: Data-parallel pools should shift the best ratio toward decode, since dp2 attention packs more decodes per GPU than tp8.
Measured: best was 2P/6D TP4xDP2 + EP at 33.2 tok/s/GPU (concurrency 32).
sections.title: Sweep: pd-dp2

prose: Splitting every request should cost ITL headroom against the threshold arms, because each handoff stalls a decode slot.
Measured: best was 4P/4D TP8 + EP at 37.17 tok/s/GPU (concurrency 32).
sections.title: Sweep: pd-always
